correctness.rationale: For any tree the rooted conditional-innovation transformation has determinant one and pairwise uncorrelated coordinates. Its exact positive diagonal variance product gives the covariance determinant, which specializes through Fibonacci independent-set recurrences to two closed all-size formulas. The three five-vertex isomorphism classes are exhausted, all exact fractions compare strictly, and a 25-factor rational outward-bound plus a rigorous infinite-tail bound proves the limiting broom/path determinant ratio is greater than 1.0042008072. The packaged checker verifies enumerated finite cases independently. No finite check substitutes for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The generic tree-model covariance-precision factorization is explicitly credited to Loh-Wainwright and Nguyen-Berg and is not claimed original. The specific first five-vertex change of extremizing tree, all-dimensional broom/path closed determinant comparison, and strictly positive asymptotic limit form the final new claim. Comparison against actual semantic database records and the most relevant stable-set, independent-set-recursion, and graphical-model primary texts found no stronger published implication that resolves this shape comparison. Residual priority risk remains.
residual_risks: A specialized tree-model covariance determinant optimization or equivalent low-dimensional extremal table outside the inspected sources could already contain the path/broom comparison.
The current result does not classify all maximizing trees for n>=6, and its eventual comparison does not give the least n after which all brooms dominate paths.
Generic tree precision and determinant decompositions are known and have no originality status here.

value.rationale: A first-failure threshold among **all** trees through order five supplies a complete natural extremal boundary for the Euclidean covariance-ellipsoid volume of stable-set polytope vertex clouds. A nontrivial product-limit proof shows this is not an isolated tiny counterexample: the same local fork raises determinant relative to paths in infinitely many arbitrarily large dimensions. This clarifies which familiar tree shapes are not extremizers for a natural continuous metric invariant. Not merely a renamed generic tree precision identity.
